prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1229; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claimant reported a left-turn collision at an intersection and said a vehicle coming straight through struck the driver's side of their car. The claim was opened the same day and the file was assigned for review.

Entry 2: The driver is named on the policy, and the policy was in force at the time of the reported loss. Nothing in the underwriting file suggests the vehicle damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 3: Police attended the scene and confirmed the claimant was in the vehicle at the time. Two officers' notes are on file and they match the claimant's first account.

Entry 4: Photos taken at the scene confirm several details of the reported impact. The vehicle damage is consistent with the described angle and direction of the collision.

Entry 5: No independent witnesses have come forward, so the account rests on the claimant's statement, the photos, and the police report. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection records.

Entry 6: The claimant reported neck pain shortly after the collision and was seen at an urgent care clinic. No earlier injury to the same body area is known from the medical history provided.

Entry 7: The claimant has since added a few small details to the account, such as the position of the signal and the speed of the other car. The core sequence of events has stayed the same across each retelling.

Entry 8: Treatment for the neck strain followed a usual course of physical therapy and medication. Reports show steady improvement, and the treatment has tapered off as the patient recovered.

Entry 9: It is not yet clear whether the neck injury came from this crash, as the medical records and the timing of symptoms are still being reviewed. The file remains open pending the treating provider's causation opinion.

Entry 10: The claimant is not represented by an attorney and has been dealing with the adjuster directly. The file will be reviewed again once the remaining medical records are received.
